text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Experts attending the FIGO World Gynaecology & Obstetrics Congress in Copenhagen disagree about the advantages or disadvantages of hormone replacement treatment (HRT) for post-menopausal women. Danish biotechnology group Novo Nordisk, the sponsor of the congress, is a leading researcher into hormone therapy for women.

--According to ministerial sources, the Danish government is again considering imposing tax on earnings from shares in return for cuts in corporation tax as part of the draft 1998 state budget to be unveiled in late August.

--Currency unrest in south-east Asia is reportedly delaying the final purchase by Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction (PSC) of a 48 percent share in Danish shipbuilding and shipping group J.Lauritzen's Danyard.
--Germany's Landesbank Kiel has done well out with its one-year old branch in Copenhagen and is now planning further expansion in the Nordic region.

--A Sonar opinion poll shows that Danes are divided into three equal "yes", "no" and "don't know" camps as regards the European Union's Amsterdam Treaty, on which a referendum is to be held in Denmark next year.

--Denmark is the centre for an international lobby campaign by European airports to maintain duty free sales within the European Union in defiance of EU plans to scrap the system in 1999 in the interests of creating a free internal market inside the 15-member bloc.
